owner.name: Maya Chen
owner.public_bio: Founder of Ledgerline (payment rails for AI agents). Ex-Stripe infrastructure. London.

items.title: Why Ledgerline
items.text: Agents are going to buy things. Today every agent that pays for something uses a human's card with no spending policy, no audit trail, no per-task limits. Ledgerline = scoped virtual accounts for agents, policy engine, receipts. I can build all of it. I cannot sell it. Need a commercial cofounder who has actually closed SMB deals, not a consultant.

items.title: Lessons from Fennel
items.text: Fennel died for two reasons. 1) Sam was 'full-time soon' for 9 months and never was. Never again: cofounder full-time or nothing. 2) I was CEO and spent 70% of my week on board decks and investor updates. I never want to be CEO again. CTO, own the product and the system, let someone who loves the room be in the room.

Me: honestly I'd give up equity for the right person. Wen: how much? Me: I'd start at 60/40. I'd do 55 if they bring real customers. Not less, I've been building this for 8 months and the core is done.

items.subject: Re: stablecoin rails?
items.text: Priya, thanks for the intro to the stablecoin folks but we stay fiat. I watched the Terra collapse take out our biggest partner at Fennel and it nearly killed us. Card rails and open banking only. That is not a 'for now' thing for me.

items.caption: Leo in his school uniform at the gate of Rosemead Primary, first day of reception. Hackney, London.

items.text: Tom: the SF thing came up again with that investor? Me: told them no move before next summer at the earliest. Leo just started school, your job is here. After July we can talk about it properly.

items.subject: Ledgerline next steps
items.text: Lena: Loved the demo. Our concern is team. If you have a commercial cofounder full-time by mid January we can take this to the partner meeting on 22 Jan. Maya: Understood. I'll have someone full-time by 15 January or I'll tell you honestly that I don't.

items.title: Recurring: Deep work (no meetings)
items.text: Mon to Fri, 08:00 to 13:00, repeats weekly. Note: 'protect this, it is where Ledgerline gets built'.

items.title: School pickup
items.text: Tue and Thu 15:15 to 15:45, repeats weekly.

items.title: Ledgerline status
items.text: Policy engine v0.3 live. Virtual account issuing via Modulr sandbox. 3 dev-tool design partners (two agent startups, one internal tooling team at a bank). Problem: dev-tool partners love it but none will pay more than 200/month. We need a vertical where agents move real money every day.

items.title: Wedge ideas
items.text: Where do agents move real money daily? Procurement. Accounts payable. Restaurants and small hospitality order from 10 to 30 suppliers a week, all by WhatsApp and invoices. An AP agent with a Ledgerline account and a spend policy per supplier is the cleanest demo of the whole thesis.

Priya: you'd need someone who knows restaurants. Me: yes. Someone who already has restaurant customers would be a dream, I'd happily build around their pilots if they're real and they'd let us test agent payments.

items.subject: Runway
items.text: Personal runway: savings cover about 14 months with no salary. Company has 120k from the pre-seed angels. I can keep my salary at zero until the round.

items.title: Cofounder must-haves
items.text: 1. Full-time, no side job, by mid January. 2. Has sold to SMBs, ideally hospitality. 3. Wants to own fundraising and the board. 4. Respects mornings as build time. 5. Okay with standard 4 year vest, 1 year cliff, for both of us. Nice to have: London based, in person 1 to 2 days a week.
Wen: still no cofounder? Me: met a few. All want to be CTO or want to do crypto. I'm tired of explaining why we don't touch stablecoins.

items.caption: Whiteboard photo: 'Agent wallet -> policy engine -> rails (cards, open banking)' with 'NO CRYPTO' circled in red.

items.subject: Intro: Jonah (Tabby)
items.text: Priya: Jonah runs Tabby, AP tooling for restaurants, ex-Deliveroo and Tide. Strong seller, 6 pilots. He's still employed. I think you two should talk.
